notes:
Top-line: SunReach (EU-headquartered online apparel & home goods retailer) wants automated ticket/email summarization + multi-label auto-tagging to reduce TAT and improve routing. Current stack: Zendesk + internal tagging rules + SFTP archival. Key problems: high ticket volume during flash sales (Black Friday-like peaks twice/yr) and noisy agent tags leading to routing errors.

POC ask: 2-week pilot on Dedicated pool or Hosted with VPC peering to validate throughput (target 120 req/s steady, 600 req/s burst), summary latency below 250ms median, tagging precision > 85% for top-10 categories. Need to demo macros/workflow integration: auto-populate Zendesk fields, suggest macros to agents, and add tags for downstream analytics.

Security/compliance: EU data residency required for tickets older than 30d; SOC2 required for vendor selection; SSO (SAML) + customer-managed KMS preferred. Legal flagged retention timeline in security questionnaire (see drive doc).

Timeline & activity (shorthand):
- 2026-01-20 created inbound lead via blog form (high volume ops)
- 2026-01-27 discovery call w/ Ava P., CTO (Marta Silva) and Head of Support (Elliot Price) — captured requirements, asked for latency & tagging KPIs; Fireflies: ff_20260211_SunReach-discovery-8b2f
- 2026-02-03 sent initial pricing + hosting options (drive deck), SE follow-up on batching suggestions
- 2026-02-18 demo: Hosted API + simple Zendesk webhook demo; spotlight on streaming vs batch for long threads
- 2026-02-24 security questionnaire submitted by SunReach (drive link) — Legal escalated retention question
- 2026-03-02 agreed to 2-week POC: ingest ~10k tickets (last 6 months), run summarization + auto-tagging, integrate suggested macros into a sandbox Zendesk instance
- 2026-03-08 POC kickoff call; SE Rafael Kim to run integration; created Jira INF-1122 for sample data ingestion issues

Customer quotes / sentiment (paraphrase):
- "We need summaries our agents can trust — not 3-line generic copy." — Head of Support
- "Peak-day reliability is non-negotiable. If it fails during sale windows, we lose revenue." — CTO

Technical notes (SE):
- Prefer open models with quantized weights but will accept Redwood-verified variants. Want routing fallback: if dedicated capacity saturated, auto-route to compatible smaller model with degraded summary length.
- Tag taxonomy: 120 raw tags today; want top-10 auto-tag first then incremental suggestions to agents. Need confidence scores per tag.
- Zendesk API limits: currently 10 req/s per account; plan to use worker pools + batching via Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Next steps (concrete):
- SE to deliver POC runbook + test data checklist by 2026-03-11 (Rafael)
- Legal to review retention answer and propose contract language (Jordan + Legal)
- Run 2-week POC: measure summary latency distribution, tagging precision/recall, macro suggestion acceptance rate

Open questions for customer / Redwood:
- Can Redwood provide a pre-built Zendesk macro template and sample automation manifest? (customer asked)
- Confirm whether Dedicated reserved pool needed for peak-day SLA or hosted with burst is sufficient
- Clarify support window for on-call during POC spikes

Stance: High priority if POC meets latency and tagging quality. Procurement timeline tied to April budget cycle.
short_description: Mid-market EU e-commerce team evaluating Redwood for ticket summarization + auto-tagging integrated with Zendesk. POC scheduled, security + retention are blockers.
